subtype: Approach: learning the routines with a written list [Action]
passage: On the first morning at the school in Haifa, Yosef got lost twice between classes and arrived late with his face hot. That night he took a clean page of his diary and wrote a list: bell times down the left side, room numbers in the middle, teachers' names on the right. He drew a small map of the corridor with arrows. Next day he glanced at the page before every break. Vera looked over and asked, "Is that a map?" "It's my cheat sheet," he said. By Thursday he did not need to look at all. The worried knot in his stomach had loosened.

qa.q: What three things did Yosef list in his diary?
qa.a: Yosef listed bell times, room numbers and teachers' names.

qa.q: What was Yosef feeling on the first morning, and how did the list change it?
qa.a: Yosef felt anxious and embarrassed after getting lost, and the list reduced the unknown so the knot in his stomach loosened. 🙂

qa.q: What alternative approach could Yosef use, and why?
qa.a: Yosef could ask a teacher for a class buddy or ask Vera to walk with him. A friendly guide gives company as well as directions.

qa.q: How might Vera see Yosef's cheat sheet?
qa.a: Vera asked whether it was a map and seemed curious, so Vera likely sees a smart way to cope with a new school.

grounding: A boy writes the bell times, room numbers and teachers' names in his diary, and reducing the unknown makes him less worried and stops him getting lost.

subtype: Approach: learning the routines with a written list [Action]
passage: On his second day at the residential school, Siddharth got lost twice. The science lab was not where he thought, and the bell for the maths period rang while he stood in the wrong corridor. That evening in the hostel study room he opened his diary and asked Usha ma'am, the house mother, for the timetable. He copied the bell times down the side, then room numbers, then the teachers' names next to each subject. "Room 14: Maths: Joshi sir." He drew a tiny map of the second floor. Usha ma'am watched him fill two pages. The next morning he checked the diary at each bell. He did not get lost once, and his shoulders came down from around his ears.

qa.q: How many times did Siddharth get lost on his second day?
What do Siddharth's shoulders coming down suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: He felt calmer and less worried once the diary took the guessing out of each change of class.

qa.q: What else could help Siddharth in his first week?
qa.a: He could ask a classmate to walk him to the rooms he finds hardest, so the diary and a friend together fill the gaps.

qa.q: How does the diary look to Usha ma'am?
qa.a: Usha ma'am sees a new boy calmly solving his own problem, and is probably pleased to watch him settle.

grounding: It shows a new boy writing bell times, room numbers and teachers' names in his diary to reduce the unknown and stop getting lost.

subtype: Approach: learning the routines with a written list [Action]
passage: Jeevan joined our Class 6 on a Monday. I'm Nikita; I sit behind him. On the first day he walked into the art room when we had music, and the whole class laughed. On Tuesday I saw him with a little notebook open during every change of period. Inside it were the bell times, the room numbers, and the teachers' names written in neat capitals, even Mr. D'Souza's, which is hard to spell. Before each bell he looked at it, then went. I don't know if he was scared or just careful. But on Wednesday, when a new supply teacher asked where the music room was, it was Jeevan who told her, not us.

qa.q: When did Jeevan walk into the art room by mistake?
qa.a: On the first day, when the class had music.

qa.q: What might Jeevan have been feeling when the whole class laughed?
qa.a: He may have felt embarrassed and anxious to avoid another mistake, though Nikita can only guess from what followed.

qa.q: What else could help Jeevan besides his notebook?
qa.a: A classmate could offer to walk with him for a few days, which would take some of the pressure off and help him make friends.

qa.q: How might the class's laughter feel to Jeevan compared with Wednesday?
qa.a: Being laughed at on Monday probably stung, so being the one who knew the way on Wednesday must have felt like a small win.

grounding: It shows a new boy keeping a written list of bell times, rooms and teachers to reduce the unknown and stop getting lost.
